sections.overview: The spotted redshank breeds in far-northern Eurasia and winters mainly in Africa and southern Asia.
sections.identification: Breeding adults are black with white spots; winter birds are pale, and unlike the common redshank it has a longer, finer bill and no broad white wing-bar.
sections.habitat: It nests in northern bogs and marshes near taiga or wooded tundra; on passage and in winter it uses estuaries, muddy wetlands and lagoons.
sections.diet: It wades in shallow water for small molluscs and aquatic insects.
sections.behavior: It is mainly a passage migrant in Britain, though small numbers winter in western Europe.
sections.reproduction: It lays about four eggs in a simple ground nest near water; both adults incubate.
sections.ecology: Its close Tringa relatives include the greenshank, lesser yellowlegs and wood sandpiper; see their profiles for comparison.
sections.conservation: It is globally assessed as Least Concern, although the BTO reports declining passage counts in Britain since a late-1990s peak.
